LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation and advice.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#18 Genie in a Bottle Song
•	 TR#19 Travel with me Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 After-School Activities (P.E.M.2)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 2: sets of Memory cards 
(P.4.2 + P.4.7)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 7: Country Bingo boards + 
Attraction cards (P.4.7) + counters
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 8: Country flash cards (P.4.3)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 4: Country flash cards (P.4.3)
•	 Big Book
•	 Magic Creature and Places (A3) and Magic Creature

•	 Day 5 stickers (1 per child)
•	 Crayons or pencils
BEFORE CLASS
Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have completed 
at least half of the recommended activities up to this point.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (10’)

2.– STUDENT STORYTELLING WITH CHANGES  
(PP.2-8) (10’)
Have your students choose new variables and tell the first half 
of the story themselves. Please see the section on storytelling 
in the Warm-Up Routines Index.
3.– WORKSHEET: WHAT’S WRONG WITH THESE 
PLACES? (PP.8-9) (9’)
What’s Wrong with These Places?
Australia
Egypt
India
8
What’s Wrong with These Places?
South Africa
Madagascar
Brazil
9
MATERIALS
•	 Crayons or pencils
NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying, “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
This worksheet depicts six countries, each of which is paired 
with two attractions. Ss must identify which pairings are incorrect 
and which are the correct ones. For this worksheet, the Ss will 
do most of the talking, but you should model the task first.
Start by saying, “I didn’t go to Egypt to see the polar bears. 
I went to Egypt to see the pyramids.” and have the Ss cross 
out the polar bears under Egypt and circle the pyramids.
Continue by pointing to Australia and asking a S, “Did you 
go to Australia to visit the Eiffel Tower?” and the S must 
respond, “I didn’t go to Australia to visit the Eiffel Tower. I 
went to Australia to see the kangaroos.” Then all the students 
draw an X over the image of the Eiffel Tower and draw a circle 
around the correct item (in this case, kangaroos). Then the S 
who answered asks the S sitting to their right a question about 
the next picture and they should then respond accordingly, using 
the structure mentioned before.
> Follow-Up
Point to one of the countries and ask a S, “Which country 
did you go to and what did you visit there?”. Elicit, “I went to 
India and I visited the Taj Mahal.” Try to ask the Ss who need 
some extra practice of this structure.

TARGET LANGUAGE
I didn’t go to Egypt to see the polar bears. I went to Egypt 
to see the pyramids.
I didn’t go to Australia to visit the Eiffel Tower. I went to 
Australia to see the kangaroos.
I didn’t go to India to visit the Great Wall. I want to India to 
visit the Taj Mahal.
I didn’t go to South Africa to see the Statue of Liberty. I 
went to South Africa to see the elephants.
I didn’t go to Brazil to see Mount Fuji. I went to Brazil to 
see the Amazon rainforest.
I didn’t go to Madagascar to go to Patagonia. I went to 
Madagascar to see the lemurs.

> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission), 
say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots

of games in Mission 4, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 5 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic.
The point of this activity is to practise after-school activities 
in a fun way. Ss have to stick the stickers and identify what 
each character did. Model the task by looking for the stickers, 
sticking them, and answering the questions.
Have Ss open pp.24-25 (sticker section) and say, “Let’s see 
what Pam and Paul and their family have been doing lately!”. 
Point to rectangle number 71 and ask, “What number is this?”. 
Ss should respond, “It’s number 71!”. Say, “Can you find number 
71 on the sticker sheet? Who is it?”, and elicit, “Here it is! It’s 
Pam.”. Next, point to the Pam in the top row bubble and ask 
them, “What did she do on Tuesday?”. Elicit, “Pam went to a 
swimming lesson on Tuesday.”
Follow the same procedure for stickers 71-78, asking the 
questions indicated in the key.
We recommend making this activity more dynamic by turning 
it into a competition to answer the questions as fast as possible. 
If you can’t finish the whole activity, tell the Ss that they can 
continue at home.
KEY
Sticker 71: What did she do on Tuesday? Pam went to a 
swimming lesson on Tuesday. 
Sticker 72: What did he do on Thursday? Dad went to 
football practice on Thursday.
Sticker 73: What did she do on Wednesday? Mum went 
to an art class on Wednesday.
Sticker 74: What did she do on Friday? Grandma went to 
a yoga class on Friday.
Sticker 75: Did Grandpa go to a yoga class on Saturday? 
No, he didn’t.
Sticker 76: Did Dad go to basketball training on Thursday? 
No, he didn’t.
Sticker 77: Did Paul go to a music lesson on Monday? 
No, he didn’t.
Sticker 78: Did Mum go to a dance class on Wednesday? 
No, she didn’t.

6.– ACTIVITY 2: WHERE DID THEY GO? (8’)
P.4.2
P.4.2
Egypt
P.4.7
> How to Play
In this activity Ss will create sentences about the characters 
going to different countries and visiting different monuments.
> Warm-Up
Prepare three piles of cards face down, one with characters 
(P.4.2), one with countries (P.4.2) and the other with monuments, 
animals and food (P.4.7). Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s 
find out where the characters travelled to last year!”. Model the 
activity for the Ss by drawing a card from each pile. If possible, 
model both a correct and an incorrect combination of cards.
For example:
•	 Take Pam, Egypt and Mount Fuji from each pile, and 
say, “Pam didn’t go to Egypt to visit Mount Fuji; she 
went to Japan to visit Mount Fuji.”
•	 Take Pam, Egypt and the Pyramids, and say, “Pam 
went to Egypt to visit the pyramids.”
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Ss take a card from each pile and identify whether the 
character went to the right country to visit the monument.
If, for example, they take Dad, India and Taj Mahal, they should 
form a sentence using the following structure: “Dad went to 
India to visit the Taj Mahal.” 
If they don’t find a match, they will have to state the correct 
activity for that country. For example, if a S takes Mum, South 
Africa and Taj Mahal, they will say, “Mum didn’t go to South 
Africa to visit the Taj Mahal; she went to South Africa to see 
the elephants.”

You can use prompts and actions where necessary if the Ss 
are unable to remember the different countries and monuments.
NOTE: to play this activity, it is not necessary to consider 
the actual places that the characters visited in the story. For 
cards with food items, you should change the target language 
accordingly “Mum didn’t go to China to eat curry, Mum went 
to India to eat curry.”. Same goes for “go on a safari”, “have a 
barbecue”, “eat noodles”, etc. 
> Follow-Up
Once every S has had a turn, take a correct combination of 
cards and ask the Ss, “Where did Grandma go to and what did 
she do there?” to which the Ss should reply, “Grandma went 
to India to visit the Taj Mahal.”
Then, show an incorrect combination and ask, “Did Grandma 
go to South Africa to visit the Taj Mahal?” to which Ss should 
reply, “No, she didn’t. She went to India to visit the Taj Mahal.”
7.– ACTIVITY 7: COUNTRIES MEMORY LOTTO (8’)
P.4.7
South Africa
China
Argentina
P.4.7
P.4.7
> How to Play
For this game, Ss must match the attractions on the Memory 
cards (P.4.7) with the countries on their Bingo boards (P.4.7).
> Warm-Up
Show the Ss one of the boards. Point to a country and ask, 
“Where did you go? What did you see or visit there?” to which 
Ss should reply for example, “I went to Brazil to visit Christ the 
Redeemer.” Ask a few more Ss about the rest of the countries 
on the board.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Give each S one Bingo board and place the Memory cards 
face down in the middle of the table. Introduce the activity by

saying “Let’s talk about the places we travelled to and what 
we saw there!”
To play, a S turns over a memory card which shows something 
you can see or do in a certain country.
If it is a match the S must say, “I went to South Africa to see 
elephants. It’s a pair. Can I have a counter, please?”
If it is not a match, they must say, “I didn’t go to South Africa 
to see kangaroos; I went to South Africa to see elephants. 
It’s not a pair.” 
Adapt the target language (eat, go, see, visit) as needed.
> Follow-Up
When a S finishes their board or time has run out, ask a S 
about their board by saying, “Where did you go and what did 
you do there?” to which the S should reply, “I went to India to 
visit the Taj Mahal, to Canada to see polar bears and to Spain 
to visit the Alhambra.”
8.– ACTIVITY 9: NUMBERS (VERSION 2) (4’)
P.E.M.3
55
This game is based on the traditional game Snap!
Mix the Numbers (P.E.M.3.) with the jokers by getting the Ss 
to say, “Mix, mix, mix” and encouraging them to say “Stop!”. 
Take the whole deck and start turning over the cards and 
putting them in the middle. The Ss should state whatever number 
comes out by saying, for example, “It’s number 62.”. Whenever 
a joker is turned over, they should say, “Snap!”. Try to keep a 
good pace so that the game is more interesting.
The first S to say, “Snap!” gets all the cards in the middle, and 
the next round starts. The game is over when it’s not possible 
to put more cards in the middle. The winner is the S with the 
most cards.

BONUS
ACTIVITY 8: TRAVEL WITH ME SONG (TR#19) 
> How to Play
Get the Ss to stand up in a circle and distribute the flash 
cards of the ten countries mentioned in the song. Introduce the 
activity by saying, “Let’s sing and travel around the world!”. The 
Ss should sing the song and perform the related movements. 
When a country is mentioned, the S holding that flash card 
should step forward and turn around in the circle showing their 
classmates the card before returning to their place.
TRAVEL WITH ME SONG
C’mon, c’mon
Come with me 
(make a “come here” motion with your arm by 
stretching it out and then bringing it towards yourself)
Let’s travel the world and see what we can see 
(hold out arms at your sides like an airplane and then

hold your hand above your eyes as if protecting them 
from the sun and look around)
We can see kangaroos in Australia
And the Statue of Liberty in America
We can see elephants in Africa
And visit the pyramids in Egypt
(chorus)
We can see polar bears in Canada
And visit the Alhambra in Spain
We can visit the Great Wall in China
And the Eiffel Tower in France
(chorus)
We can visit Big Ben in England
And the Taj Mahal in India
So many places for us to see
So come on, come on, travel with me
ACTIVITY 4: WHERE ARE YOU FROM?
> How to Play
Ss must ask and answer questions about where they and their 
classmates are from according to the flash cards they pick up.
> Main Activity
A Ss chooses a Country flash card (P.4.3) and keeps it a secret 
from the rest. The group then asks, “Where are you from?”. 
The S should give clues using the following structures:
•	 Where I’m from people speak…
•	 Where I’m from you can see…
•	 Where I’m from people eat…
•	 Where I’m from you can visit…
Ss must guess their classmate’s country by asking for 
example, “Are you from Australia?” to which the S should 
reply, “Yes, I am,” or “No, I am not.” Make sure that every S 
participates either by taking a country or by asking questions. 
As it can take a long time for all Ss to have a go at this activity 
we recommend that you take a note of any Ss that didn’t get 
a go so they can go first the following day.
